name: Pyruvic acid peel
summary: A clinic-applied superficial acne peel using an alpha-keto acid; evidence is a handful of small studies.
lead: A pyruvic acid peel is a superficial chemical peel that uses pyruvic acid, an alpha-keto acid, applied to the skin by a clinician to loosen and shed the outer layers. It is described in dermatology literature as a keratolytic peel used mainly in acne vulgaris.

name: Phenol-croton oil peel
summary: The classic deep surgical-grade peel for wrinkles and tightening, now used in gentler low-phenol versions.
lead: The phenol-croton oil peel is a deep chemical peel used for facial resurfacing, wrinkle reduction and skin tightening. The classic Baker-Gordon formula, published in 1962, was long considered the standard for deep facial resurfacing.

name: Chemical reconstruction of skin scars
summary: Spot-applying strong TCA acid into individual acne scars; studied in small trials.
lead: Chemical reconstruction of skin scars (CROSS) is a focal technique in which a high-concentration trichloroacetic acid (TCA) solution is applied to the base of individual atrophic scars, such as ice-pick acne scars, rather than to the whole face.

name: Skinvive
summary: Microdroplet hyaluronic acid injected into the skin for texture and glow; early-stage evidence.
lead: Skinvive (Juvederm Volite VYC-12) is a hyaluronic acid injectable made by Allergan that is placed in the skin itself in many small microdroplets to improve skin quality, rather than to add volume. It belongs to the Juvederm range of hyaluronic acid products.

name: Profhilo Structura
summary: A high-concentration hybrid hyaluronic acid injectable aimed at restoring cheek and facial fat volume, backed so far by small case series.
lead: Profhilo Structura is an injectable hyaluronic acid (HA) product made by IBSA Farmaceutici, marketed as a medical device for restoring facial volume and contour, particularly in superficial fat compartments of the face such as the lateral cheek. It is a variant of the original Profhilo "skin remodelling" product and uses the same patented NAHYCO hybrid technology, which combines high- and low-molecular-weight HA into thermally stabilised complexes without chemical cross-linking.

name: Profhilo Body
summary: A hybrid hyaluronic acid skin booster for body skin laxity, studied so far in small single-arm trials.
lead: Profhilo Body is an injectable hybrid hyaluronic acid (HA) product from IBSA Farmaceutici, marketed as a medical device for improving skin laxity and roughness on the body, such as the upper inner arms and the backs of the hands. It uses the NAHYCO hybrid technology, which forms cooperative complexes from high- and low-molecular-weight HA.

name: Rejuran HB
summary: A polynucleotide skin-booster injectable with almost no published human data.
lead: Rejuran HB is a polynucleotide (PN) injectable used in aesthetic medicine as a skin booster. Polynucleotides are chains of nucleotides, and the term covers DNA and RNA, which also have uses beyond cosmetics. Rejuran products are referred to in the literature as part of a family that includes Rejuran S and Rejuran HB Plus.

name: Juvelook
summary: A Korean PDLLA-hyaluronic acid biostimulator injected for tear troughs, folds and skin texture, supported by small studies and case reports.
lead: Juvelook is an injectable poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) product made by VAIM Inc. of Seoul, South Korea, used in aesthetic medicine as a skin booster and collagen-stimulating agent. Published reports describe a PDLLA and hyaluronic acid hybrid formulation, with variants named Juvelook Volume and Juvelook GLAM.

name: Lenisna
summary: A PDLLA booster with almost no published efficacy data; the main literature is a safety consensus on rare vision-loss complications.
lead: Lenisna is the name of a poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) injectable used in aesthetic medicine. The only source identified is a 2026 expert consensus on safe injection technique and the management of visual impairment caused by PDLLA-HA200, a next-generation injectable combining PDLLA microspheres with non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid as a carrier.

name: Aesthefill
summary: A Korean PDLLA microsphere biostimulator with one randomised trial against hyaluronic acid and a large body of technique papers.
lead: AestheFill is an injectable poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) microsphere product made by REGEN Biotech of Seoul, South Korea. It contains PDLLA microspheres with carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) as a suspending agent, supplied as a lyophilised powder that is reconstituted with sterile water before injection, and is described as biocompatible, biodegradable and biostimulatory.

name: Pure Polynucleotide (PDRN)
summary: Injectable salmon-DNA-derived 'skin booster' borrowed from wound-care medicine; promising lab and orthopaedic data, but little controlled evidence for facial appearance.
lead: Polydeoxyribonucleotide (PDRN) is a mixture of single-stranded DNA fragments that was first isolated from human placenta for pharmaceutical use in Italy and is now mainly purified from salmon or trout sperm. It is used in wound-healing and tissue-repair medicine and, particularly in parts of Asia and Europe, as an injected cosmetic 'skin booster' marketed for skin quality, scars and aging signs.
claims: PDRN regenerates skin and improves texture beyond hyaluronic acid boosters
PDRN is a safe, non-immunogenic salmon product

name: Volite / Volift
summary: Juvéderm Volite is a low-concentration hyaluronic acid gel injected into the skin for smoothness and hydration; trial data exist but are mostly single-arm and manufacturer-linked.
lead: Juvéderm Volite is a crosslinked hyaluronic acid (HA) gel (VYC-12, also marketed as Skinvive) injected intradermally to improve skin quality attributes such as surface smoothness and hydration. It is described as providing longer-lasting effects at a lower HA concentration than traditional fillers.

name: Restylane Vital / Skinboosters
summary: Galderma's small-dose hyaluronic acid injections placed in the skin to improve elasticity and texture; the longest-studied skin booster, mostly in small clinical studies.
lead: Restylane Vital, part of the Restylane Skinboosters line, is a stabilised hyaluronic acid-based gel of non-animal origin (NASHA) injected into the dermis in small amounts to improve skin quality such as elasticity and smoothness. Restylane is made by Galderma and was the first hyaluronic acid filler approved by the US FDA for cosmetic injection into facial tissue.

name: Redensity
summary: Teoxane's 'Redensity' hyaluronic acid products (RHA Redensity and Teosyal Redensity) for lines and under-eye hollows; includes a randomised 52-week perioral trial.
lead: Redensity refers to hyaluronic acid (HA) products from Teoxane, including RHA Redensity (a 'resilient' HA filler) and Teosyal PureSense Redensity 1 and 2.

name: Sunekos
summary: Italian injectable that mixes hyaluronic acid with amino acids as a skin 'biorevitalising' booster; supported mainly by small manufacturer-linked trials.
lead: Sunekos is a commercially available mixture of hyaluronic acid and amino acids in an alkaline solution, injected for skin aesthetics. Registered studies have evaluated it for face photoaging, the area around the eyes and skin laxity of the inner thighs, knees and arms.

name: Exosome facial
summary: Skin-quality treatment using cell-derived vesicles after microneedling or laser: only small early studies exist and no exosome product is FDA-approved.
lead: An exosome facial is an aesthetic procedure in which a product marketed as containing exosomes, small membrane-enclosed vesicles released by cells, is applied to or introduced into the facial skin, commonly after microneedling or laser treatment, with the aim of improving skin quality, texture and scarring.  Exosomes are one subtype of extracellular vesicle, and the source cells for aesthetic products vary: mesenchymal stem cells, adipose tissue, umbilical cord, and plants have all been named in trial registrations.

name: Mesogun
summary: Handheld multi-injector for mesotherapy that delivers small intradermal doses of hyaluronic acid, vitamins or PRP; device-specific evidence is sparse.
lead: A mesogun is a handheld, spring- or pressure-driven injector used in mesotherapy to deliver many small intradermal injections of a solution in quick succession, typically across the face.  The solutions used in aesthetic practice include hyaluronic acid, vitamins, and, in some clinics, platelet-rich plasma.

name: PRP (platelet-rich plasma) injections
summary: Centrifuged-blood injectable used for skin and under-eye rejuvenation; trial evidence is mostly from knees, not faces.
lead: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is a concentrate of plasma prepared from a person's own blood. The blood is centrifuged to remove red cells while retaining platelets, which contain growth factors and cytokines thought to aid tissue healing.  The concentrate is then injected or applied to the target area. In aesthetic medicine it is marketed for wrinkles, skin rejuvenation and hair growth, and it is sometimes combined with microneedling in what is popularly called a 'vampire facial'.
claims: PRP may give better under-eye results than tear-trough filler

name: PRF (platelet-rich fibrin)
summary: Fibrin-clot cousin of PRP used in dental surgery and tried by forum users for under-eye circles; no facial trials found.
lead: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), also called leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF), is a derivative of platelet-rich plasma in which a person's own platelets and white blood cells are held in a fibrin matrix. Blood is drawn without anticoagulant and centrifuged immediately, producing a clot layer between platelet-poor plasma and red cells.  A 2006 series of papers by Dohan, Choukroun and colleagues described it as a 'second-generation platelet concentrate'.
claims: PRF is a strong treatment for dark under-eye colour and eye bags
PRF filler for dark circles did not work for some users
PRP or PRF serums can be made at home from one's own blood

name: Liquid facelift
summary: Marketing term for filler-based non-surgical facial rejuvenation; the literature is mostly reviews, with no controlled trials found.
lead: 'Liquid facelift' is a marketing term for non-surgical facial rejuvenation that uses injectable fillers, often hyaluronic acid, to restore volume and contour in several areas of the face in one session.  The term is also used in one 2018 case series for a different technique: water jet-assisted liposuction used alongside surgical rhytidectomy.

name: Collagen induction therapy
summary: Microneedling: controlled skin punctures meant to trigger collagen repair; the best-studied use is scars, with more modest evidence for wrinkles and texture.
lead: Collagen induction therapy (CIT), widely known as microneedling, dermarolling or skin needling, is a cosmetic procedure in which a device bearing fine needles repeatedly punctures the skin to create controlled micro-injuries . The intended result is stimulation of the skin's repair processes and new collagen and elastin formation, as an alternative to ablative treatments that remove the epidermis .
claims: Microneedling boosts collagen and improves scars.
Microneedling avoids the pigmentation risk of lasers and peels.
Microneedling with PRP or topicals gives better results.

name: Aqualyx
summary: A deoxycholate injectable sold in Europe for localized fat; its use for facial hollowing in forums goes beyond any clinical evidence.
lead: Aqualyx is a gel-like aqueous solution of sodium deoxycholate, developed in Italy by Professor Pasquale Motolese and commercially available since 2009, marketed by Marllor and sold to doctors and nurses trained in intralipotherapy . It is CE-marked in the European Union and used for localized subcutaneous fat .
claims: Aqualyx gives a permanent hollow-cheek look.
Self-injected or imported product is equivalent to clinic treatment.

name: Follicular unit extraction (FUE)
summary: Hair transplant method that removes follicles one by one from the donor scalp, avoiding a linear scar at the cost of longer surgery.
lead: Follicular unit extraction (FUE) is a hair restoration technique in which individual follicular units are removed from the donor scalp with small punches, instead of excising a strip of skin, and transplanted to areas of hair loss . The term was coined in a 2002 paper that introduced the approach as minimally invasive surgery for hair transplantation .

name: Follicular unit transplantation (FUT)
summary: Strip-harvest hair transplant: a scalp strip is removed and dissected into grafts, leaving a thin linear donor scar.
lead: Follicular unit transplantation (FUT), also called strip harvesting, is a hair transplant technique in which a strip of scalp is taken from the donor region and divided under stereo-microscopes into follicular units for implantation . Wikipedia describes strip excision as replacing plug grafts in the 1980s, with microscopic dissection of strips developed in the late 1980s .

name: Direct hair implantation (DHI)
summary: A FUE variant that places grafts with a pen-style implanter; clinics promote precision, but independent evidence is scarce.
lead: Direct hair implantation (DHI) is a hair transplant technique using the Choi implanter pen to implant follicular units without separate pre-made incisions . It follows FUE-style extraction of follicles from the donor scalp.

name: Sapphire FUE
summary: FUE variant using sapphire-tipped blades for recipient incisions; promoted as finer, with little independent evidence yet.
lead: Sapphire FUE is a follicular unit extraction hair transplant in which recipient sites are made with sapphire blades instead of steel . Grokipedia says the blades are sharper and finer, which may allow denser placement, less bleeding, faster healing and less visible scarring ; these are unverified descriptions from an AI-generated source.

name: Choi implanter pen
summary: A pen-style implanter that places each graft as the incision is made; clinics promote it, but published comparisons are absent.
lead: The Choi implanter pen is a hand-held device used in hair transplantation to make the recipient-site opening and place a harvested follicular unit in a single step. It is most often associated with the technique marketed as Direct Hair Implantation (DHI), described as a variant of follicular unit extraction (FUE) in which grafts are loaded into the pen rather than placed into pre-cut slits.

name: Scalp reduction
summary: Surgical removal of bald scalp to shrink the bald area; an older hair-restoration adjunct with sparse modern evidence.
lead: Scalp reduction is a surgical procedure in which a segment of hairless or thinning scalp skin is cut out and the remaining hair-bearing scalp is pulled together and sutured, reducing the area of bald skin. In the dermatologic literature it was described as an adjunct to hair transplantation as early as 1980.

name: ARTAS robotic system
summary: A FDA-cleared robot that harvests donor hairs for FUE; it automates extraction, and published outcome data were thin in the sources.
lead: The ARTAS system is a computer-assisted robotic device for hair restoration, made by Restoration Robotics. It uses image guidance to identify and extract individual follicular units from the donor scalp in follicular unit extraction (FUE).

name: NeoGraft
summary: An automated suction-assisted FUE device; reported FDA-approved in 2009 with little published outcome data.
lead: NeoGraft is an automated device used for follicular unit extraction (FUE) in hair transplantation. Wikipedia describes it as the first robotic surgical device FDA-approved for hair restoration, in 2009, while noting limited detail. Grokipedia describes it as using pneumatic pressure to extract and deliver grafts without twisting or pulling.
